prompt:
Draft a procedure for hazard identification and risk assessment at a multi-story warehouse with automated storage and retrieval systems (AS/RS), forklift traffic, manual picking areas, loading docks, and battery charging stations. Address routine, non-routine, and emergency scenarios. Align with ISO 45001 clause 6.1.2.

Return a single JSON object with EXACTLY these fields:
- document (string): the complete procedure or document text
- sections (string): structured sections of the document
- clauseRefs (string): ISO clause references addressed

End your response with exactly one line: ANSWER: <your JSON object>
response:
{
  "document": "Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment Procedure for Multi-Story Warehouse with AS/RS

1. Purpose
This procedure establishes a systematic approach to identifying hazards, assessing risks, and implementing controls in alignment with ISO 45001 Clause 6.1.2. It applies to all activities within the multi-story warehouse, including automated storage and retrieval systems (AS/RS), forklift traffic, manual picking zones, loading docks, and battery charging stations. The goal is to eliminate or minimize occupational health and safety risks during routine, non-routine, and emergency operations.

2. Scope
Applies to all employees, contractors, and visitors operating in or accessing the warehouse facility. Covers all physical, mechanical, chemical, ergonomic, and psychosocial hazards associated with warehouse operations.

3. Responsibilities
- Safety Officer: Leads hazard identification, risk assessment, and documentation.
- Department Heads: Ensure team participation in assessments and implementation of controls.
- AS/RS Technicians: Provide technical input on automated system hazards.
- All Personnel: Report hazards and unsafe conditions immediately.

4. Hazard Identification Methods
Hazard identification shall be conducted using the following methods:

4.1 Routine Operations
- Walkthrough inspections (daily/weekly)
- Job Safety Analysis (JSA) for repetitive tasks (e.g., manual picking, forklift loading)
- Equipment maintenance logs review
- Employee feedback and near-miss reporting

4.2 Non-Routine Operations
- Pre-job risk assessments for maintenance, system upgrades, or cleaning of AS/RS
- Permit-to-work systems for confined space entry or hot work near charging stations
- Temporary layout changes (e.g., during inventory rotation)

4.3 Emergency Scenarios
- Scenario-based drills (fire, system failure, chemical spill, structural collapse)
- Review of incident reports and emergency response plans
- Assessment of egress routes, emergency stop functionality, and communication systems

5. Risk Assessment Methodology
Use a 5x5 Risk Matrix (Likelihood x Severity) to evaluate each identified hazard:

Likelihood: 1 (Rare) to 5 (Almost Certain)
Severity: 1 (Minor) to 5 (Catastrophic)

Risk Level = Likelihood x Severity
- Low: 1–4
- Medium: 5–9
- High: 10–25

All High and Medium risks require immediate control measures. Low risks are monitored.

6. Hazard Categories and Examples

6.1 AS/RS Systems
- Pinch/crush points during automated movement
- Malfunctioning sensors or software errors
- Falling loads due to rack instability
- Electrical hazards from control panels

6.2 Forklift Traffic
- Collisions with pedestrians or racks
- Overturning on ramps or uneven surfaces
- Improper load balancing
- Blind spots and inadequate signage

6.3 Manual Picking Areas
- Repetitive motion injuries (shoulder, wrist)
- Slips, trips, falls from elevated platforms
- Poor lighting or cluttered aisles
- Improper lifting techniques

6.4 Loading Docks
- Vehicle-to-dock plate mismatches
- Falls from dock edges
- Pinch points during trailer securing
- Exposure to weather and noise

6.5 Battery Charging Stations
- Hydrogen gas accumulation and explosion risk
- Acid spills and chemical burns
- Electrical shock from faulty chargers
- Overheating and thermal runaway

7. Risk Control Measures (Hierarchy of Controls)

7.1 Elimination: Remove hazard (e.g., redesign layout to eliminate manual lifting)
7.2 Substitution: Replace hazardous process (e.g., use lithium-ion batteries instead of lead-acid)
7.3 Engineering Controls: Install guardrails, sensors, automatic shut-offs, ventilation
7.4 Administrative Controls: Training, signage, work procedures, job rotation, maintenance schedules
7.5 PPE: Gloves, safety glasses, steel-toe boots, hearing protection (last line of defense)

8. Documentation and Review
- All hazard identification and risk assessments documented in the Safety Management System (SMS)
- Risk register updated quarterly and after any incident, change in equipment, or process
- Review conducted annually or after major incidents
- Records retained for minimum 5 years

9. Training and Communication
- All personnel trained on this procedure and hazard reporting mechanisms
- Posters and digital alerts display current high-risk areas and controls
- Monthly safety meetings include hazard update briefings

10. Emergency Response Integration
- Emergency stop buttons accessible at all AS/RS and charging stations
- Evacuation routes clearly marked and unobstructed
- Spill kits and eyewash stations located near charging stations
- Coordination with fire department for AS/RS fire scenarios

11. Continuous Improvement
- Use of near-miss reports and incident investigations to refine risk assessments
- Benchmarking against industry best practices
- Employee suggestion program for hazard control ideas

12. References
- ISO 45001:2018 Clause 6.1.2
- OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178 (Forklift Safety)
- NFPA 70 (National Electrical Code)
- ANSI/ITSDF B56.1 (Industrial Truck Safety)

Approved by: [Safety Director Name]
Effective Date: [Date]
